text:
maya: Heads up — customer reported streaming responses truncating mid-event for a subset of Safari 16 users behind an edge CDN (Akamai). They say reconnection happens but partial 'data:' frames are lost. Full logs + repro below.

ben: ugh. any common headers missing? sounds like CDN or h2 multiplexing issue.

maya: minimal repro: SSE endpoint works fine for chrome and firefox. safari loads initial chunks then stalls, browser logs show EventSource closed with no network error. Network tab shows 200 then connection terminates with short Content-Length-ish chunk.

liam: can you paste response headers?

maya: sure — captured from origin (our service) and from edge (Akamai) side-by-side: 

Origin headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
X-Accel-Buffering: no
Vary: Origin, Accept-Encoding, Authorization
```

Edge (Akamai) observed headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: max-age=0
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
```

maya: note the Vary header is missing at the edge and Cache-Control different. Also a couple of traces show edge responding with a 304 to preflight in some flows.

liam: missing Vary=Authorization is a red flag — if edge caches an SSE response and strips Authorization vary, token rotation or auth headers will cause cached partial stream for other users. Akamai config often has 'no-cache-sse' rules but might be overridden.

ben: could be also H2 -> H1 downgrade or http/2 multiplexing causing premature stream close. Safari has historically had issues with H2 server push and long-lived responses. Which infra region?

maya: customer in EU, hits our edge POP in Frankfurt. They said they rotated API tokens midway and saw client-side reconnect loop 401 -> then reconnect but only partial payload.

infra-lead: probable sequence: 1) edge cached initial SSE response without Vary Authorization 2) customer rotates token (auth changes) 3) edge serves cached connection snapshot to new client -> chunk mismatch -> safari sees malformed stream and drops connection.

liam: repro steps I used locally against our staging edge: 
1) start SSE endpoint that emits a message every 2s
2) hit endpoint from Safari + curl behind a simulated CDN that strips Vary header
3) after ~10s, rotate token or simulate 401 and allow reconnect

Result: Safari shows intermittent partial events, EventSource.onerror fires, then reconnect but initial event lost. Chrome tolerates it.

maya: attaching a short snippet we asked the customer to run to capture behaviour (they ran in console):
```
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.test/stream?user=123', { withCredentials: true });
es.onmessage = e => console.log('MSG', e.data);
es.onerror = e => console.log('ERR', e);
```

ben: Possible mitigations: 
- Ensure edge doesn't cache SSE: set Cache-Control: private, no-transform, no-cache and add "Surrogate-Control: no-store" for some CDNs.
- Make Vary header include Authorization + Origin so edge won't serve others.
- If CDN supports it, disable http/2 buffering for SSE endpoints or force h1 proxying.
- Add a small heartbeat comment every N seconds (":\n\n") to keep proxies/prolong timeouts.

liam: also recommend short-term workaround: vendor polyfill for Safari that does incremental XHR streaming fallback (EventSource polyfill) — but that's heavier. Better to fix edge rules.

maya: customer asked if we can verify origin logs for partial writes — I pulled token rotation logs: 
```
[2026-03-12T10:12:05Z] conn=abcd1234 sent chunk 512
[2026-03-12T10:12:07Z] conn=abcd1234 token=tok-old AUTH_OK
[2026-03-12T10:12:09Z] token-rotation user=123 new_tok=tok-new
[2026-03-12T10:12:10Z] edge=fra1 cache_hit=true cache_key=/stream?user=123
[2026-03-12T10:12:10Z] edge=fra1 served cached_chunk=1/??
```

maya: seems like edge cached initial chunk and served it.

infra-lead: action items: 
- @liam can you open vendor ticket with Akamai and ask them to confirm whether their POP can return cached SSE slices? ask for config to honor Vary: Authorization and to disable ASI buffering for SSE endpoints.
- @ben can you push a quick origin header change to add Surrogate-Control: no-store and no-transform + Vary: Authorization on the SSE route (staging first).
- @maya can you share customer curl / repro so we can validate after changes?

ben: I'll push the header change to staging in ~15m and include a short smoke test script.

liam: also send them this note about CloudFront/Cloudflare gotchas: some CDNs will convert chunked streaming into buffered responses unless explicitly told not to, usually via "Cache-Control: no-transform" and specific CDN behavior flags.

maya: customer follow-up: they tried adding ?_nocache=1 and saw better luck — suggests cache key/matching issue. we'll coordinate.

support-bot: Reminder: ticket #CS-10987 linked to this thread. Priority: High.

infra-lead: good. once ben's staging change is live, ask customer to retest and capture network traces. If still flaky, escalate with Akamai with packet captures from POP.

maya: will update ticket and ping when staging change deployed. thanks all :thumbsup:
